The Met Office reports that England saw just 5.6mm of rainfall up to 30 July â just 8% of its long-term meteorological average for the month and less than half of the previous record of 13.4mm set in 1911.

For Wales it was 7.9mm of rainfall, also 8% of its long-term average for the month and almost a third of the previous record of 22.6mm, again set in 1911.

Heat health alerts are in place across most of England until at least 09:00 BST on Wednesday.

Amber alerts indicate a rise in deaths of vulnerable people and increased demand on health services are likely, while yellow alerts indicate these are possible.

News.title: Man admits transporting Scottish woman's body in suitcase, Greek police say
News.content:
Greek police say a man has admitted transporting the body of a Scottish woman in a suitcase to an abandoned building.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, days after she was reported missing.

Local officers launched an investigation with cooperation from authorities in the US, the UK and Scotland, and now say they have arrested a 26-year-old man - the BBC understands he is from Afghanistan.

The force said he was brought to police headquarters on Thursday where he "confessed to his actions". He was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, robbery and weapons offences, but the exact charges have yet to be finalised under the Greek legal system.

News.title: Body of mountaineer Nirmal Purja recovered after Pakistan avalanche
News.content:
Prince William said he was "truly saddened to hear of the tragic death" of Purja, who he said "served with distinction" as a soldier before "becoming one of the greatest mountaineers".

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: "Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."

Naila Kiani, a spokesperson for the Alpine Club of Pakistan which is involved in the rescue efforts, told BBC's Newshour programme on Saturday that her organisation feared all members of the group were dead, and that Purja had led many expeditions she was on.

Praising his leadership skills, she described him as a "very experienced climber and fearless".

Teams in Pakistan have been searching for the climbers on the world's 12th-highest summit since Thursday's avalanche on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. Also known as Nims, he rose to prominence in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world's mountains with peaks above 8,000m in 189 days - smashing the previous record by more than seven years.

He became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released two years later.

At the time, he said: "It has been a gruelling but humbling six months, and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity."

Purja served in the British military for 16 years, 10 of which were spent in the special forces, and he was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering.

Purja, who lived with his wife and three-year-old daughter in Hampshire in southern England, said he was also the first Gurkha to climb Everest while serving in the British military.

In his last post on X, published on Monday, he said he had not intended to climb Broad Peak.

"Initially, the plan was to climb just G2," Purja wrote, referring to Gasherbrum II, another peak in the Karakoram mountain range.

But right before he set off for Pakistan, he realised if he also managed to climb Broad Peak while he was there, he would have only one more mountain to conquer before becoming the "first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen."

An eight-thousander is a mountain that rises more than 8,000m above sea level.

"This wasn't planned," Purja wrote. "But opportunities don't scream: they whisper to those already working in silence."

"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down. I take zero mountains for granted," he wrote.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives.

One of Broad Peak's deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

News.title: Ballot paper for Clacton by-election is longest in British electoral history
News.content:
The longest ballot paper in British political history is costing four times as much to print than regular ballot papers, the local council has said.

The list for the Clacton parliamentary by-election, which was prompted by the resignation of Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, is 90cm (3ft) long.

When people unfold the paper, they will find it is longer than most adults' arms.

Tendring District Council chief executive Ian Davidson - who is the acting returning officer for the by-election in the Essex constituency - said organising the vote had been "manic".

People have already started returning postal votes to town hall and most registered voters will go to polling stations on 13 August.

Davidson said: "We've logistically been looking at the size of the ballot paper, how we fold it to get it into the envelope so we can send it out to our postal voters [and] how we manage the polling stations."

News.title: Teenager dies after 'medical episode' at Kendal Calling festival in Cumbria
News.content:
A teenage girl died at the Kendal Calling festival in the early hours of the morning, police have said.

The 17-year-old suffered a medical episode at about 02:15 BST and was pronounced dead at the scene, according to Cumbria Police. The force asked people not to speculate about the circumstances of the incident.

It added officers were looking into the circumstances and wanted to speak to anyone who was in the area of the Calling Out tent and the Big Wheel around the time of the girl's death.

A spokesperson said: "Officers are particularly keen to speak with a group of women who alerted first responders to the girl after becoming concerned for her welfare."

They said the girl's family had been informed and were being supported by specialist officers.

The force asked people not to speculate, saying it could have a "significant impact" on the family and friends involved.

"We would ask that the investigation be allowed to take its course."

News.title: Three in hospital after fire and crush at festival in London
News.content:
Three people were taken to hospital after a fire and crush at the entrance of a festival.

Organisers of Ghana Party in the Park, also known as Shattafest UK, at Copthall Playing Fields in Barnet, London, said the event was stopped following a "major incident" at about 18:00 BST on Saturday.

The Metropolitan Police said a fire had started near the gates, which meant they were closed temporarily.

A crowd built up, and there was a surge when the gates reopened, it said.

Organisers said the decision to end the festival was made on health and safety grounds.

They said in a statement the day had been "one of the most difficult" in the event's history and called what happened "deeply upsetting".

News.title: Four arrested over hate crime attack on ship crew
News.content:
Three men have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a Filipino crew member of a cargo ship was attacked in what police described as a hate crime.

Two other men, both also from the Philippines, were also assaulted during the attack involving a large group of people in Avonmouth, near Bristol, on Friday evening.

Police have arrested two men aged 19 and 45, as well as a 17-year-old boy, on suspicion of attempted murder and confirmed they had received reports of racist language being used during the incident.

They remain in custody, as well as a 38-year-old woman arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

The U.S. dollar weakened sharply Monday against the Japanese yen after U.S. President Donald Trump and Japan’s finance minister confirmed both sides had intervened in markets.

Before late last week, the dollar was trading above 163 yen, touching 40-year highs. After regulators were suspected of stepping in, it fell below 160 yen.

Early Monday, after the official announcement of the intervention, the dollar dropped about 1% to 156.34 yen. That’s a big change for the exchange rate.

The yen's prolonged weakness against the dollar has been a source of frustration for Tokyo. Since Japan imports so much of what it consumes, a weak currency pushes prices higher, increasing inflation.

Efforts earlier this year to raise the value of the yen against the dollar did little to budge the exchange rate.

Last week, the U.S. side was suspected of lending a hand. When asked why Washington was helping, Trump said Sunday that “We have a good relationship with Japan. We’re very strong —- very, very strong financially — and they are, you know, they have a weakening yen, and they wanted a little bit of help, and we’re always there for Japan. Japan’s been very good to us, with the exception, of course, of Pearl Harbor.”

Trump said the U.S. got “financial benefit” out of the intervention, calling it a “signal of friendship.” “It’s also good for the world economy.”

In Tokyo, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama issued a statement confirming the intervention, saying the finance ministry had purchased yen in coordination with the U.S. Treasury Department.

The move followed a joint statement last year and “countered excessive volatility and disorderly movements in the Japanese yen in recent months,” it said.

It added that the ministry would not hesitate to act further if necessary.

The judge who granted the right to play another year of college sports to some athletes whose eligibility ran out last school year issued a new order Sunday that makes clear that does not include football players who signed pro contracts this summer then had a change of heart.

U.S. District Judge Charlotte Sweeney responded to an NCAA request for clarity about her Friday ruling that granted a fifth year to athletes who graduated high school in 2022 and were not included in the new NCAA rule that allows five seasons of eligibility for Division I players.

That decision, she said, still stands, but has no impact on other NCAA rules, including its prohibition on players signing pro contracts, then coming back to college.

The ruling, as first written, had the potential to upend the upcoming college football season, where teams are starting camp planning on the so-called “five for five” rule to take effect beginning next fall.

Extending it to players this fall granted hundreds a chance to return to school. In the direct aftermath of the decision, some media reports were listing players on NFL and CFL rosters who were signaling they’d be open to returning to school.

But that appears to be off the table after Sweeney's clarification that said there are no changes to the NCAA's rules regarding pros; no exceptions over when athletes can enter the transfer portal; and no impact on elements of the landmark House lawsuit settlement, which dictates how many players teams can put on rosters and how much schools can pay them.

The rulings out of U.S. District Court in Denver figures to impact sports differently. Football teams, for instance, have already started practice for this season, while baseball doesn't start for a while.

In making decisions, teams figure to factor the NCAA's coming appeal of Sweeney's order and whether to risk bringing back players who could then be declared ineligible if her decision is overturned.

NCAA President Charlie Baker issued a statement after Sweeney's initial ruling came out Friday, saying the ruling was potentially chaos-inducing and a reason Congress needs to pass the Protect College Sports Act. That bill, being considered in the Senate, includes lawsuit protection for the NCAA over eligibility rules, the likes of which they defending in several courts around the country.

President Donald Trump said Sunday that the strike on Iran he ultimately called off would have been the largest of its kind in decades.

“It was going to be a massive attack,” the Republican president told reporters aboard Air Force One. “It was going to be an attack that would have been, by far, the biggest attack since World War II.”

His comments followed a Truth Social post on Saturday in which Trump wrote that the U.S. military was “locked and loaded” for what he cast as an unprecedented campaign against Iran. But, he said, he decided to hold back after appeals from Iran and several Middle Eastern allies, who suggested a deal was within reach.

“I was asked to by Saudi Arabia, by UAE, and by Qatar, and by Iran,” the 80-year-old president said on Sunday. “We were all set to go, but when the allies ask to call it off, you gotta sort of say ‘well let’s see.’”

Trump said the agreement would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and address Iran’s nuclear program. “So, we’re holding it,” he said. “We’ll just see.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump said on Sunday that the canceled attack on Iran would have been the biggest 'since World War II.' He said the attack was called off after Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE intervened ( AFP via Getty Images )

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signaled that the U.S. military remained primed for action, writing on X Sunday evening that the Pentagon “was ready to go — and remains ready — at levels not seen since World War 2.”

Iranian media denied that Tehran had asked for the strikes to be called off. “Trump the fool has run out of steam,” a semi-official state news agency posted, according to CNN. Iran’s acting defense minister, Seyyed Majid Ibn Al-Reza, also accused the U.S. of “psychological and cognitive warfare,” according to a state media post on X.

The Saudis, however, did step in, according to Axios. The outlet reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called Trump on Saturday to voice concern over the president’s planned strikes — which could have targeted energy sites — and urged him to de-escalate.

Throughout the war, Trump has repeatedly invoked cataclysmic rhetoric when threatening Iran, including warning in April that “a whole civilization will die.” At the same time, he has frequently paused the fighting to open the door to negotiations, only to resume hostilities when those efforts came up short.

open image in gallery The passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital artery of global trade, has emerged as a major sticking point in negotiations. Pictured: A drone view shows vessels in the waterway on June 15 ( Reuters )

The latest round of fighting erupted after a brief truce established by a memorandum of understanding collapsed last month, with the passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz — a vital artery of global trade — emerging as a major sticking point.

On Sunday, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said that negotiations between Iran and Oman over the strait are in their “final stages,” according to the official news agency IRNA.

The war, which has now ground on for five months, has left 18 U.S. service members dead and hundreds more wounded, the Pentagon has said. Over 3,000 Iranians have died, Reuters reported in March, citing the U.S.-based non-profit HRANA.

open image in gallery Iran’s acting defense minister accused the US of 'psychological and cognitive warfare,' according to a state media post on X. Pictured: Motorists in Tehran drive past a large billboard pledging revenge against Trump on July 27 ( AFP via Getty Images )

The conflict has also rattled the global economy, sending oil prices higher as traffic through the strait dwindled to a trickle.

Multiple recent polls indicate the war is deeply unpopular in the U.S. In an AP-NORC survey last month, about two-thirds of Americans said the conflict has not been worth fighting.

According to an NBC News report late last month, Trump himself is “exasperated” by the lack of progress in ending the war. “There was not a real strategy for how long or what they should do to get to the endpoint,” an unnamed ally of the president told the outlet. “He did not intend this to be a long, drawn-out war.”

In response to this report, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt told The Independent at the time that Trump “is not going to stand by as they break the [memorandum of understanding], kill our soldiers and fire at our ships in the Strait.”

July is typically the warmest month of the year - but this month could be the hottest ever in the United States.

Temperatures have been above average for 260 million Americans in recent weeks, meteorologist Ben Knoll wrote in a social media post Friday.

New York City experienced its hottest day since July 2012 and Utah’s Salt Lake City saw its hottest day since record-keeping began 152 years ago.

Similarly dangerous heat events fueled by climate change are becoming the “new normal,” Steven Cohen, director of the sustainability management program at Columbia University, told NPR.

This year’s supercharged El Nino climate pattern has also been a factor.

open image in gallery People cool themselves with an ice-cold water bottle during the Great American State Fair in Washington, D.C., two days before the Fourth of July. This month has seen record temperatures and deadly heat - making it one of the worst Julys ever ( Getty Images )

El Nino brings warmer and drier weather throughout the northern and central U.S., with wetter and more humid conditions in the South. It’s also helped to form multiple deadly heat domes this July, with more on the way.

Heat domes are high pressure systems in the Earth’s atmosphere that trap heat over areas, lasting for days or even weeks.

It’s the length of these phenomena that makes them deadly and domes have been tied to at least 70 deaths in Mississippi, Illinois and other states this summer, according to a tally of local health data from The Washington Post.

New Jersey reported 29 deaths during the first of two oppressive East Coast heat domes on the Fourth of July weekend.

The first canceled celebrations and resulted in buckling rail lines.

But the threat is not yet over.

Another heat dome is set to bake the West this weekend, fueling wildfire threats and pushing temperatures near 120 degrees in California and Arizona, according to AccuWeather.

“Temperatures above 100 degrees are common in the deserts during midsummer. However, this strengthening heat dome will push highs 10-20 degrees above the historical average into early August,” AccuWeather senior meteorologist Alex Sosnowski wrote Thursday.

open image in gallery People walk and bike in New York City earlier this month as dangerous Canadian wildfire smoke fills the skies. Wildfire smoke has been linked to developing cancer ( AFP/Getty )

And more frequent and severe life-threatening heat events are expected to hit the U.S. in coming summer seasons, climatologists warn.

“We know that heat waves are becoming more intense, they’re lasting longer, they’re covering larger areas than they used to because of human-caused climate change,” Daniel Swain, a climate scientist with University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources, told The Associated Press.

That likely means rising death tolls. Heat is already the deadliest weather condition in the U.S., causing 2,000 deaths each year, Yale research shows.

The invisible killer can strain organ function and forces the heart to work harder to pump blood.

Increased heat also can mean worsened drought and more of the tinderbox conditions needed to fuel major wildfires that send toxic, cancer-linked smoke hundreds of miles away.

That’s already happened this month, too, with air quality becoming hazardous for much of the Great Lakes, Midwest and Northeast.

“Extreme heat and wildfire smoke each carry major risks, especially for people with chronic health conditions including heart disease,” Dr. Manesh Patel, chief of the division of cardiology at Duke University School of Medicine, said in a statement. “The combination of the two is extremely dangerous.”

At least five survivors of sexual abuse at the hands of Harrods owner Mohamed al-Fayed are victims of human trafficking, the Home Office has confirmed.

The survivors, whose experiences include both international and domestic trafficking, have received conclusive grounds decisions from the National Referral Mechanism (NRM), the UK’s official framework for identifying victims of modern slavery, including human trafficking, forced labour and servitude.

Once a potential victim is referred to the NRM, the Single Competent Authority (SCA), which is part of the Home Office, processes the referral and decides on whether to officially recognise the individual as a modern slavery victim.

On 29 April 2026, it was reported by the BBC that one victim had received a positive conclusive grounds decision, after reporting abuse suffered at the hands of Mohamed al-Fayed and his brother, Salah.

Since then, all four members of an advocacy group for Fayed survivors called No One Above have also received conclusive grounds decisions that they are victims of modern slavery: Justine, Elizabeth, Margo and Isabella, all pseudonyms.

While these four have been confirmed by the Press Association (PA), it is understood that there are more survivors who have also received positive conclusive grounds decisions.

Their cases date back as early as the Nineties, while the most recent incidents took place after the 2010 sale of Harrods.

One survivor told PA they were recruited to a false role within Harrods, while two were hired for a legitimate role and then selected for abuse off the shop floor.

Another survivor was employed as a domestic worker for Al Fayed after being recruited via a letting agency called Hyde Park Residence.

All five survivors were referred to the NRM by the charity Unseen UK.

open image in gallery Mohamed al-Fayed (Daniel Hambury/PA credit) ( PA Archive )

This reporting framework allows victims to receive appropriate support and provides the government with vital data about modern slavery in the UK.

Justine worked at Harrods for more than three years in the Nineties, and was trafficked and abused during this time.

She told PA she felt “shell-shocked” when she received the conclusive grounds decision in June that she had been a victim of modern slavery.

Justine said: “It’s not something I realised was happening to me at the time, so it’s all part of this journey that we’re on now in reliving this experience, and actually really understanding what happened to us, which is very difficult.”

She added: “But it’s a really significant thing, getting that decision, seeing it in writing that you were a victim of modern slavery and trafficking is very… it’s really shocking to read.”

Justine told PA that this is “concrete confirmation” from the Home Office that Fayed survivors were victims of human trafficking and that the scope of experiences was wide: from domestic to international trafficking, from those who worked at Harrods to those not involved with Harrods at all.

She said this is “very significant”, because Harrods’ position has been that the abuse was just the actions of “one bad man”, and that there is nothing they can do now he is dead.

Justine said: “These decisions illustrate that that is not the case at all.”

open image in gallery The Harrods department store in Knightsbridge, central London (James Manning/ PA credit) ( PA Archive )

Elizabeth was also a Harrods employee and received a conclusive grounds decision that she was a victim of modern slavery in May.

She told PA that all the survivors in the Fayed case are victims of human trafficking, because it was all one system that recruited, exploited and silenced victims.

She said: “Everybody connected with this case is a trafficking victim, because it was all one system. You can’t say that victim A wasn’t trafficked and victim B was. I think there’s this persistent misunderstanding, possibly within the Metropolitan Police themselves, which is scary, that trafficking only involves being moved across international borders.

“There have been positive conclusive grounds trafficking decisions in cases where the trafficking occurred within the Harrods building.”

Margo was a domestic worker for Al Fayed after the sale of Harrods, and was recruited via a letting agency called Hyde Park Residence.

She received a positive conclusive grounds decision that she was a victim of human trafficking in July.

Margo told PA that she had not felt like a victim of trafficking “because really I didn’t know what trafficking was, especially domestic trafficking”.

She said Fayed’s trafficking network went “so beyond Harrods”.

“This was Balnagown [a Scottish property], it was Saint-Tropez, it was Fayair [a private jet company], it was Fulham Football Club, it was Hyde Park Residence.

“Everywhere he went he had enablers, and everywhere he went he had the capacity to abuse. All of his residences, all of his businesses,” she added.

Margo said she did not originally come forward because she did not work at Harrods.

She said: “There has just been so much emphasis put on Harrods to the point where I believe that there are so many more victims that haven’t come forward because they believe that it’s solely a Harrods issue.

open image in gallery ‘Everywhere he went, he had enablers,’ said one Fayed victim ( PA )

“I know of one other Hyde Park Residence victim, but there has to be hundreds more somewhere.”

Isabella worked in the chairman’s office at Harrods in 2001. She received her conclusive grounds decision that she was a victim of trafficking in May.

She told PA: “I think one thing that the public doesn’t understand is they think this was one bad man, but he couldn’t have done what he did without Harrods processing women to him and silencing them afterwards.

“And it wasn’t just Harrods, obviously. It was any entity that Al Fayed owned or had control of.

“It was his yachts, his aviation business, the Ritz Paris, his properties all over France and Monaco, it went as far as the States and the UAE – anywhere that man touched.”

It was not just Mohamed Fayed either, she said, but “a wider network of perpetrators”.

Isabella added: “We are not aware of any negative decisions in this case, and there have now been many self-initiated referrals through Unseen.”

More than 400 allegations of sexual misconduct have been made against Fayed, dating between 1977 and 2014, including sexual assault, rape, sexual exploitation and human trafficking.

The Met Police are investigating at least 156 victims who contacted them directly, including 21 who came forward before Fayed died in 2023 at the age of 94.

The investigation, known as Operation Cornpoppy, is looking at people who may have facilitated or enabled Fayed’s crimes. Four people have been questioned to date, 19 months after the investigation opened.

The Home Office has been approached for comment.

More than one in 10 householders who are currently living with a hosepipe ban do not intend to abide by it, according to a survey.

Some 11% of households said they did not intend to fully abide by the ban – while 5% said they did not yet know, the YouGov poll of more than 4,200 adults commissioned by the Press Association found.

Some 10% of householders said they would report a neighbour using a hose in their garden while a ban was in place and 71% said they would not, with the remainder unsure.

Seven water companies – Affinity Water, Anglian Water, Cambridge Water, Southern Water, South East Water, Thames Water and South West Water – have introduced the restrictions – officially known as a “Temporary Use Ban” – affecting 23 million customers, or around 40% of England’s population.

Overall, just half of households (49%) said they supported a hosepipe ban in their local area, while 35% said they opposed the restrictions.

A significant number of responses from those polled involved the belief that those on a meter should be able to use as much water as they needed because they were paying for it.

Other reasons given for ignoring a ban were concerns about fruit and vegetables going to waste because they were too difficult to water with a watering can, and to support wildlife in the garden.

Households subject to a ban can use a watering can, and using a hosepipe is still allowed to water food crops at home or on an allotment when using a watering can is not practical.

A drip irrigation system for a garden is also allowed as long as it is fitted with a timer and pressure-reducing valve and delivers water directly to the soil rather than spraying it into the air.

The ban does extend to using a hosepipe to clean a car or fill a paddling pool or domestic swimming pool.

Other householders raised concerns about their water supplier’s wider performance, with one saying: “I pay an extortionate amount for my water. It is not my problem that water companies would rather give their CEOs ridiculous amounts of money instead of building new reservoirs.”

Another said: “How does a first world nation not have the infrastructure to support no rain for a month?”

The bans come as almost a third of England – including parts of the South East, Midlands and North West – languish in “prolonged dry weather” status, with only the North East and Yorkshire still seeing “normal” conditions for the time of year.

Last week, the Environment Agency declared seven areas of central, eastern and southern England – around half of the country – as officially in drought as a result of very low rainfall and high temperatures.

Last year, Yorkshire Water reported savings of up to 10% in household consumption when their hosepipe ban was in place, while Anglian Water has reported a 9% reduction in demand since its ban was implemented last month.

A Water UK spokeswoman said: “We are incredibly grateful to customers for doing their bit to protect our environment and preserve our water supplies.

“Some parts of the country have seen demand for water rise by more than a third.

“Water companies are working round the clock fixing leaks, moving water across regions and running treatment works flat out to keep supplies flowing, and we urge all customers to use water wisely.”

An Environment Agency spokeswoman said: “A hosepipe can use 1,000 litres an hour – which is more than a family-of-four will use in a day.

“These short-term bans allow companies to conserve their supplies as we don’t know when this drought will end.

“We are grateful to people for following the restrictions, where in place. The less water we use, the more stays in the local environment, which is vital for the health of our rivers and wildlife.”

Consumer Council for Water chief executive Mike Keil said: “We know hosepipe restrictions are frustrating for some people, but water companies have a duty to act when sustained hot, dry weather and increased demand for water threaten both the environment and the security of water supplies needed for essential use.

“However, asking customers to play their part means water companies must be playing theirs too. Water saving is a shared responsibility and when customers see their water company failing to get a grip on leakage, it understandably drains their own motivation to save water.”

News.title: Leeds come from 2-0 down to beat Liverpool in pre-season friendly
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
For many the 100m is the Blue Riband event the one everyone wants to watch and the race that steals all the headlines. For these Commonwealth Games, however, tonight’s mile race is the one that has grabbed all the attention – and it is not hard to see why.

Josh Kerr, fresh from his new world record of 3:42.66 (a time that beat a mark that had stood since 1999) takes on fellow Scot Jake Wightman and Australia’s new superstar Cameron Myers. Three great runners over a distance that evokes sepia-tinted memories of Roger Bannister and the seminal four-minute mark.

Some of you may be wondering why the mile is back at an international event. Well, Seb Coe, the president of World Athletics and someone who broke the mile record three times, says the race distance is easy to understand and resonates with fans. And, coming on the back of Kerr’s world record, who can argue with him?

This is the first time the mile has been run at the games since 1966 and the hope is that tonight’s final matches the Miracle Mile run in 1954. Earlier that year Bannister broke the four-minute barrier, only for Australia’s John Landy to go lower with a time of 3:58.0 soon after. The Games in Vancouver were the first time two sub-four minuters had gone head-to-head. And the race didn’t disappoint – Bannister beating Landy with a time of 3:58.8 minutes. The Australian also ran under four minutes, making it the first time two men had done so in the same race.

Obviously all three of the expected main protagonists will go well under four minutes, but if they can recreate the drama of the 1954 final then we’ll have a race to savour.

Stay here for all the action with the gun set to go off at 8.55.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

Sports.title: Cape Verde hero Vozinha, 40, ‘jets in to complete transfer to new club with World Cup goalkeeper set for second U-turn’
Sports.content:
VOZINHA has jetted into Chile to complete his move to Colo-Colo.

The Cape Verde hero, 40, agreed to join the Chilean side after shooting to fame at the World Cup.



Vozinha produced an epic display in his country’s World Cup opener, producing several saves in a 0-0 draw with eventual winners Spain.

The veteran then conjured further excellent performances against Uruguay, Saudi Arabia and Argentina as his nation defied the odds.



Following Cape Verde’s 3-2 defeat to Argentina, Vozinha’s future came under the microscope.

The experienced stopper found himself out of contract following a spell at Portuguese second-tier side Chaves.

It appeared that Colo-Colo had won the race for his signature, even announcing the transfer.

But doubt was dramatically cast upon the move as a reporter claimed that Moroccan side Berkane wanted to hijack the deal, with the goalkeeper apparently ready to U-turn on his move to Chile.

Transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano has assured fans that Vozinha will in fact be signing for Colo-Colo.

And Romano even posted a picture of Vozinha on the plane to Chile, ready to complete the move.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Vozinha’s Instagram following skyrocketed during the tournament as he became a global cult hero.

But his new club will not be able to capitalise on his fame by selling “Vozinha” shirts.

League rules are set to prohibit use of the name on the back of the keeper’s top.

Instead Vozinha, full name Josimar Jose Evora Dias, will have to wear either “Evora”, “Dias” or “Evora Dias”.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino could have earned salary rivalling Haaland, Lewis Hamilton and Steph Curry if World Cup sale went ahead
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO could have been in line to earn a staggering salary comparable with the likes of Erling Haaland, Lewis Hamilton and Steph Curry had his dastardly plan to sell off a chunk of the World Cup succeeded.

The unpopular Fifa president plunged world football into chaos earlier this week with his plan to create a new subsidiary, the Fifa Forward Enterprise.



Had the plan been given the green light, the Fifa Forward Enterprise would have been in charge of Fifa’s money-making channels for its biggest events, including the World Cup.

Infantino, 56, had planned to flog a 20 per cent stake in the new sister company to private investors for a mooted $4.2 million (£3.1m).



The plan was scrapped, however, after Uefa nations including England threatened to BOYCOTT the World Cup.

Infantino earns a salary of around £2.6m as Fifa president, although this figure was thought to have roughly doubled last year following bonuses.

A new role as commissioner of the Fifa Forward Enterprise would likely have banked the Swiss former lawyer a much bigger sum.

It is expected that Infantino would have moved into the position following the end of his final term as Fifa president in 2031.

According to The Times, the role was expected to land a similar salary to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who pockets around $64m (£47m) per year.

This eye-watering sum would have brought Infantino in line with some of sport’s biggest superstars.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Per Capology, Manchester City superstar Haaland earns around £45.5m per year if he achieves the bonuses laid out in his contract.

And according to Spotrac, Ferrari icon Hamilton is paid $60m (£44.5m) by the Formula 1 powerhouse.

Curry, meanwhile, is set to pocket $62,587,158 (£46.3m) from the Golden State Warriors in the upcoming season.

Patrick Mahomes‘ contract extension with the Kansas City Chiefs will see him take home $64m (£47m) a year from 2027.



In the wake of his plan collapsing, Infantino is facing a Fifa revolt.

The Fifa president is likely to be asked to step down at a council meeting after he finally bowed to pressure and axed his lucrative project.

Sports.title: Shocking moment Leigh Griffiths’ footie star brother ‘storms into stand and attacks fan in crowd’ after being subbed off
Sports.content:
THIS is the shocking moment that Leigh Griffiths’ footie star brother stormed into the stands and appeared to confront a fan.

Paul Tansey, 40, is the brother of the ex-Celtic star and has plied his trade in the semi-pro ranks of Scottish football for the majority of his career.

6 Credit: PENICUIK ATHLETIC FC

6 Credit: PENICUIK ATHLETIC FC



He signed for Hawick Royal Albert of the East of Scotland League 18 months ago and has established himself as a key member of the squad under boss Kenny Aitchison.

The Borders outfit won the Third Division last season and were taking on Premier Division side Penicuik Athletic in the preliminary round of the Scottish Cup yesterday at Montgomery Park.



With two minutes remaining of normal time and the scoreline at 1-1, Tansey was subbed off.

As he was walking towards the away side’s dugout, Tansey took his shirt off and then made a beeline for the home end, jumping over a wall and up the steps to angrily confront a supporter.



Two members of staff had to pull him away and when he returned to pitchside, the referee brandished a red card.

It’s understood the fan had been goading Tansey, who used to play for Penicuik, throughout the game and made a personal comment towards him just as he was substituted.

6 Credit: PENICUIK ATHLETIC FC

6 Credit: PENICUIK ATHLETIC FC



Albert boss Aitchison described the incident was unacceptable and revealed the club was dealing with the matter internally.

He said: “We’ve had a chat after the game and this morning after everything calmed down.

“It’s being dealt with internally.

“We have never had any incident with him and he’s always been a good trainer and he treats staff and younger players well.”

Sports.title: Man Utd and Sunderland U16s erupt in mass brawl with punches flying during pre-season tournament
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED and Sunderland’s Under-16 stars were involved in a mass brawl during a pre-season tournament this weekend.

The Red Devils were in action against the Black Cats in Ballymoney on Friday for the SuperCupNI.



United won the semi-final game 1-0 to advance to the final of the pre-season event.

Manu Soares’ stunning goal on the half volley was enough after an assist from Jaice Fore.



But after the full-time whistle a huge fight broke out between the players as officials were forced to get involved.

According to spectators, the brawl kicked off when a Sunderland player kicked a United rival on the ground shortly after the game finished.

Footage of the incident shows both sets of player pushing and shoving one another as tensions boiled over.

Some players then started grabbing each others’ shirts with one Sunderland star pushed to the ground.

The brawl started to dissipate before smaller fights broke off as on United player was seen throwing a punch before both youngsters fell over.

The rest of the squad rushed in to break up the violence as officials struggled to get a hold of the situation.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Eventually things cooled off as the two teams walked away and into the dressing room.

No cards were issued to any of the United or Sunderland players in the footage that circulated on social media.

United went on to book a final spot with Mexican side Tigres, who they beat on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

The Red Devils lifted the Premier Globe trophy after Ben Lyne cancelled out Tigres’ opener in the second half.



In the shootout, Marley Irving made an important stop with the score at 4-4 before Joseph Deighton netted the decisive spot kick to win it.

Sports.title: Championship captain refuses to play to force Wrexham transfer as manager warns ‘he’d better hope they pay’
Sports.content:
WREXHAM are closing in on Preston North End captain Ben Whiteman – who has come under fire for “crossing the line”.

SunSport understands that the Welsh Hollywood club have offered around £2.5m for the 30-year-old midfielder.



The Lilywhites skipper is pushing for a move, leading him to skip the club’s pre-season friendly against Stockport County.

Tensions boiled over following Preston’s 1-0 loss, with manager Paul Heckingbottom raging at Whiteman’s conduct.



Heckingbottom said: “We’ve been in regular conversations in the last few days, and Ben knew there was a line I didn’t want him to cross.

“Unfortunately he has, and you can’t have that.

“My priority now is the players that are here and the players who want to play for us, and represent the club.

“Also Craig (Hemmings, owner) will have an issue with that, and Peter, because they pay the wages and things.

“There’s a valuation on him. I just hope for Ben’s sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it, otherwise he’s put himself in a really sticky situation.”

“He’s made his bed, I’m not bothered, as long as I get another player.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Hit by a shortage of available first-team players, Preston’s friendly against Barcelona at St George’s Park on Monday was cancelled.

SunSport understands Heckingbottom wanted to avoid risking key players with the season starting next week.

Wrexham are keen to add another central midfielder to provide competition for Matty James and Ben Sheaf after signing 13 players last summer.

Whiteman, who came through Manchester United‘s academy, has been at Deepdale since January 2021 and has made 224 appearances.



Preston are entering their 12th consecutive Championship season after finishing 14th, while Wrexham are bidding for promotion after narrowly missing the play-offs.

Sports.title: Unseen footage shows how Argentina got Falklands flag as fan unintentionally films World Cup security breach
Sports.content:
NEW footage has emerged showing how Argentina’s controversial Falklands flag got onto the pitch moments after their victory over England.

Lionel Messi and Co broke the Three Lions’ hearts with a late 2-1 victory in Atlanta.



After the match, Argentina stars caused uproar by posing with a flag that read “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” – meaning The Falklands are Argentine” in English.

Premier League stars Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martinez were both seen holding the flag up alongside ex-Tottenham midfielder Giovani Lo Celso.



Social media user Clara Houssay attended the match.

And more than a fortnight on, she realised that she had captured the moment that the flag made its way onto the turf on video.



Her clip clearly features the banner being lobbed down from the mob of joyous Argentine fans.

Lo Celso is the player that can be seen running over to grab it, before some of his team-mates join in.

Argentina’s flag provoked fury in England given the 1982 conflict over the islands that cost hundreds of lives, and that inhabitants have since voted overwhelmingly to remain British.

Hothead midfielder Leandro Paredes subsequently doubled down, claiming that the Falklands “will always be Argentine”.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Goalkeeper Emi Martinez praised his team-mates for “playing with a knife between their teeth” and added that England stars “didn’t feel the same way”.

But quizzed if the Falklands conflict had played its part in their motivation, Martinez was not convinced.

He is quoted as saying, in his native Spanish, “I don’t think it’s because of that. It’s in the past. I wasn’t even born.”

Fifa last month opened a disciplinary investigation against Argentina for the flag, as well as for their players’ reactions to losing the final to Spain.



Rules ban players from “using a sports event for ­demonstrations of a non-sporting nature”.

In 2014, Argentina were hit with a £20,000 fine for holding up a banner with a similar Falklands message before a match against Slovenia.

Flags referencing the Falklands were banned from the stadium by Fifa ahead of the match.

But security did not spot the message, which was written on a hotel sheet, when the Argentina fan entered the stadium.

And it was Lo Celso, rather than the stadium stewards, who was first to the object once it was launched onto the pitch.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino faces FIFA revolt as furious colleagues demand he quits over ‘shabby’ World Cup sell-off deal
Sports.content:
SHAMED Gianni Infantino was clinging to power last night as it emerged Fifa is expected to hold an emergency meeting to oust him over his plan to sell off the World Cup.

The £4.3 million-a-year boss is likely to be asked to step down at a council meeting after he finally bowed to pressure and axed his “shabby, backroom deal”.



And if he refuses to resign, then another candidate with the backing of his opponents would be put up to challenge him in next year’s spring presidential election.

One senior football source told The Sunday Times: “Infantino had it all and his reckless greed means he has now lost it. He’s an embarrassment and he’s not a lame duck, but a dead duck.”



The wave of negative publicity around the disgraced fatcat’s plan to flog off stakes in the World Cup to private investors has reportedly seen sponsors contacting Fifa in panic.

And even bank JP Morgan, which was heavily involved in the project, allegedly wants out.



Fifa was reportedly already planning to force an extraordinary general meeting before Infantino’s £15 billion “secret scheme” emerged last week.

Council members are said to have demanded an independent review into the tycoon’s unprecedented decision to lift US star Folarin Balogun’s red card during the World Cup after taking calls from Donald Trump.

The assembly could now develop into a full blown leadership challenge.

It is also possible that 41 of Fifa’s 211 member nations could call an emergency congress and stage a vote of no confidence in the shamed leader.



Potential challengers for the top job include current Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, Asian football chief Sheikh Salman, or Paris Saint-Germain boss Nasser Al Khelaifi.

Sources close to Montagliani believe he may already have 96 votes – from UEFA and Concacaf – if he challenges Infantino.

The Swiss’ plans, which involved selling 20 per cent of a new World Cup operating company to an investment firm owned by the younger brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, sparked international outrage.

Furious football chiefs and politicians have called for him to fall on his sword.



European football’s governing body Uefa accused the magnate of trying to “sell off the family silver”. It said his “shabby, backroom deal” had “lost Uefa’s confidence” and that of the wider football family.

The North and Central American Football Association Concacaf said he had “stopped putting football first” and called for a “comprehensive reckoning with this presidency”.

And on Saturday evening, Javier Tebas, president of Spain’s LaLiga, declared Infantino’s “time is up” and demanded that “world football needs new leadership”.

England great Peter Reid, 70, also joined calls for the Fifa chief to step down.



The Everton legend told The Sunday Mirror: “Infantino’s position is untenable now, people have lost faith in him…Private investors in football – that is just wrong.

“Fifa has hundreds of millions already, they should be putting more money into grassroots. That is where the money should go, instead of getting into bed with private investors.”

Infantino has so far only received backing from the associations of Qatar, Morocco and Lebanon.

Qatar hosted the 2022 World Cup and Morocco is vying to host the final in 2030.

RECOMMENDED STORIES



The Fifa president’s u-turn in the early hours of Saturday morning came after his right-hand man Carlos Coderio quit in disgust and chief operating officer Kevin Lamour announced staff had been “deceived”.

But he refused to give in to mounting pressure to resign, insisting that his intent in the coming days is “to bring all interested parties back together…in the spirit of shared interest in our game”.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino posts tone-deaf ‘Unite the World’ video after being forced to scrap hated World Cup sale
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO has posted a tone-deaf video on social media after he tried to sell off the World Cup.

The Fifa president upset most of the footballing world with his plans to sell stakes of the biggest tournament to private investors.



Infantino, 56, has since had to make a humiliating U-turn after it was widely condemned.

His unprecedented cash-grab saw entire confederations slam the decision, coming together in unity to oppose his Bond villain-like greediness.



Uefa went as far as announcing a boycott of all Fifa events in an attempt to pile the pressure on Infantino.

Football enemy no1 Infantino has not decided to retreat from the spotlight for the meantime and instead has posted a new video on his Instagram account.

The video collated memorable moments from the World Cup this summer to the song Seven Nation Army by the White Stripes.

It also showed off moments such as Norway‘s iconic rowing celebration and Lionel Messi crying at the end of the final after Argentina‘s defeat.

It also focused on the landmark achievements from the tournament, such as the record number of goals (308) and over nine million people at fan festivals.

Despite his divisive attempt to sell off a stake in the tournament, he captioned the post: “This was the Fifa World Cup 2026!

And in a video narrated by himself he said: “Football and the World Cup is not just a competition. It’s actually there to unite the world.”

And he signed off by saying: “The definition of Fifa is ‘The official happiness provider to humanity’.”

Infantino also turned the comments off on the post.



Had his sale plans plans gone ahead, then he would have been lined up for a new lifetime job as commissioner, which would have earned him almost £1MILLION-A-WEEK.

Due to the controversy surrounding Infantino, his sweep in the 2027 election has been put into serious doubt.

The Folarin Balogun red card scandal and now the humiliating withdrawal of the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) have put Uefa bigwigs on alert.



Reports suggest that Infantino could face an unexpected challenger in the election next summer.

Some names raised as potential successors include Uefa head Alexander Ceferin, PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi and Concacaf candidate Victor Montagliani.

Sports.title: Pressure grows on FIFA chief Infantino to resign as FA member pulls support
Sports.content:
Pressure grows on FIFA chief Infantino to resign as FA member pulls support

A football association from the UK has become the first to officially withdraw its support for Infantino's re-election next March, days after he U-turned on plans to 'sell off' the World Cup

View 3 Images Infantino is under pressure (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

A British football association has become the first FIFA member to officially pull its support for Gianni Infantino's re-election.

‌



The move is set to heap pressure on the Italian, who faces a severe backlash over his plans 'sell off' the World Cup. Even after cancelling the project, set to be led by a close Donald Trump ally, the FIFA President is rapidly losing support from major players in the game.

‌



The Football Association of Wales (FAW) has now reportedly made its position clear and written to FIFA to withdraw its support for Infantino's re-election.

‌



The FAW also backed a boycott of FIFA competitions orchestrated by European governing body, UEFA, in response to Infantino's plan to create a private company, open to investment, to run its headline competitions to raise billions of pounds.

It was reportedly going to be led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law. After Infantino’s plans were revealed by the media, before some high-ranking FIFA officials were even informed of his intentions, he faced a severe backlash.

UEFA, the organisation which runs European football, said it would boycott FIFA competitions until the plans were killed, and CONCACAF, its North American counterpart, also criticised the plans. Key advisers to Infantino also resigned in protest.

‌



View 3 Images Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump. (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Italian Infantino is due for re-election in March, but his future at the top of world football looks in doubt after this latest scandal.

Now, the FAW has heaped pressure on his tenure, officially withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election, according to reports.

‌



The association told Sky News it "hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr Gianni Infantino, for re-election as FIFA President for the 2027-2031 term.

"The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football.

View 3 Images Wales failed to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, but did appear at Qatar 2022 (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

"Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.

“The Football Association of Wales has written to FIFA to inform them of their position.”

Other British football associations are yet to follow suit, but all approved the UEFA boycott. However, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has gone one step further and said Infantino is ‘the wrong man’ to lead FIFA.

Sports.title: Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 2-4 LEEDS UNITED: Daniel Farke's men scored four goals in 25 second-half minutes to stun the Reds and win in the Premier League Summer Series on Sunday

View 3 Images Leeds United beat Liverpool 4-2 on Sunday as they mounted a stunning comeback (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool were left stunned as Leeds United produced a scintillating second-half comeback to come from 2-0 down and beat the Reds 4-2 in the Premier League Super Series.

‌



Fresh off the back of beating Sunderland and Championship side Wrexham, Andoni Iraola's side started on the front foot against Leeds and opened the scoring inside the first seven minutes. Luke Chambers was the goalscorer for the Reds as he smashed home from close range.

‌



Although Leeds did have some opportunities, Liverpool controlled most of the first half and ended up doubling their advantage just before the break. Florian Wirtz found the net for Iraola's side, as he finished off an excellent team move, tucking the ball home into the corner.

‌



Both teams made four substitutions at half-time and it was Leeds who came out as the stronger after the break. Brendan Aaronson capitalised on a mistake to pull one back for Daniel Farke's side on the hour mark, before Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised with a finish from inside the box.

The comeback was then complete soon after with Sean Longstaff firing home following some neat play from Aaronson. Calvert-Lewin added his second and Leeds' fourth late on to ensure the Whites were crowned as the winners of the 2026 Premier League Summer Series in the United States.

Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan READ MORE :

Mirror Football looks at the big talking points from the game...

‌



Fast Liverpool start

Liverpool scored the first goal in each of their first two pre-season friendlies and that theme continued against Leeds. Chambers, who has come into central defence since Joe Gomez suffered a new muscle injury in the 4-2 win over Sunderland last week, was the man who gave the Reds the lead.

Dominik Szoboszlai's outswinging corner was flicked on by Milos Kerkez and Chambers was there free inside the box to slam home from eight yards. In truth, it was a smart finish from the 22-year-old, who could have easily got underneath the ball but he kept his head over it before lashing beyond goalkeeper Alex Cairns.

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz scored for Liverpool against Leeds (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Huge Leeds injury blow

One of Daniel Farke's main wishes going into the fixture against Liverpool would have been to avoid any fresh injuries with three weeks to go until the start of the Premier League season. Well, unfortunately for him and the Whites Gabriel Gudmundsson hobbled off with what looked like a hamstring problem.

After going down in the opening stages with a knock, Gudmundsson carried on before being substituted in the 34th minute. The Sweden international went down appearing to hold his hamstring and was treated by the Leeds medical staff before going off and being replaced by Sebastiaan Bornauw.

Impressive Wirtz

Following a mixed first season and Liverpool's lack of attacking transfer business so far this summer, it does feel as though there is some pressure on Wirtz to produce in 2026/27. But the German showed in his first appearance back after the World Cup that he can step up and deliver after scoring the Reds' second against Leeds.

‌



It was well-worked move by Liverpool as Trey Nyoni's cross-field pass found Jeremie Frimpong who cut the ball back for Wirtz to sweep home first time from inside the box. With just seven goals in 49 matches in his debut season at the Reds, Wirtz will be no doubt wanting to improve on that total this term.

View 3 Images Wirtz had an impressive first-half

Liverpool punished for mistake

Although it's much better to iron out mistakes in pre-season, of course, Liverpool won't want to give too many goals like the one Leeds scored against them in Chicago.

‌



Milos Kerkez, who endured a difficult first season at the Reds following his move from Bournemouth last summer, gave the ball away inside his own half and Leeds punished them. Ampadu collected the ball and drove at the Liverpool back-line before playing in Aaronson and he slotted low past Giorgi Mamardashvili. It was a slack piece of play from Kerkez and he must eradicate them if he wants to be a success at Anfield.

Impressive comeback from Leeds

Leeds were much-improved after Calvert-Lewin, Aaronson, Sean Longstaff and Harry Wilson came on at half-time and they produced a scintillating comeback to stun Liverpool.

After Aaronson pulled one back, Calvert-Lewin levelled for the Whites in the 71st minute. A long-throw from Ampadu caused chaos in the box and Joe Rodon's flick-on was hammered home by Calvert-Lewin from close-range.

‌



Then, just two minutes later, the fightback was complete as Leeds took the lead for the first time in the game. Longstaff was the scorer on this occasion for Leeds, as he swivelled inside the area before drilling home.

The Whites would go on to score a fourth goal to seal the win and it came from another long throw. This time it was Bornauw who got the flick on and Calvert-Lewin was there once more to tap home from four yards.

It was an impressive comeback from Leeds and excellent character after falling 2-0 down and looking like the game was over at half-time. But Farke has instilled some belief into his side and it was on show in full flow again.

‌



Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star READ MORE :

Liverpool transfer priorities clear

If it wasn't clear before that Liverpool need to sign some players, it certainly is now. The Reds have got to bring in at least two, if not, three ready-made first-team starters before their Premier League opener against Newcastle United.

They have been among the quietest clubs in the top flight when it comes to signing players this summer and it's seen Iraola's squad look threadbare with Ibrahima Konate, Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah moving on. Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz have come in, but neither have made an appearance for the Reds so far.

The Reds are so light in a number of areas and the one that looked the weakest against Leeds was the centre-back area. While Jacquet is coming in to join Virgil van Dijk and the returning Giovani Leoni, Gomez's latest injury blow should see Iraola's side dip into the market to sign another central defender. That is a must.

Article continues below

As well as that, the Reds are lacking a serious right winger following Salah's departure, while it does still feel like they need a new left-back to help Kerkez and a high-profile central midfielder.

Sports.title: UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino legal action as FIFA chief warned not to 'destroy evidence'
Sports.content:
UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino legal action as FIFA chief warned not to 'destroy evidence'

UEFA are reported to have sent a letter to FIFA and its president, Gianni Infantino, as the aftermath of the failed FFE plans continue

View 2 Images UEFA havei issued a legal threat to FIFA president Gianni Infantino (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

UEFA have threatened under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino with legal action - and warned him against destroying any documents relating to the failed World Cup ‘sale’ plan.

‌



Controversial news emerged earlier this week that FIFA had plans to sell shares in the organisation's tournaments, which would have included the men’s and women’s World Cups, as well as the Club World Cup. The plans were met with widespread criticism, with UEFA being joined by CONCACAF and AFC in making it clear they were against such plans, which were going to be called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

‌



UEFA, following a meeting with its 55 member associations, threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions if the proposals put forward by the governing body and Infantino went ahead. The backlash eventually led to Infantino releasing a statement which confirmed the controversial scheme was to be scrapped, citing the ‘division’ within football as a reason.

‌



5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

The Telegraph has now claimed to have seen a letter which has been sent by UEFA to FIFA, as well as potential investors Joshua Kushner, Greg Maffei, JP Morgan and OpenEconomics. It has been reported that UEFA has threatened legal action and has warned FIFA not to destroy any evidence relating to the failed FFE proposals.

“Uefa hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the “proceedings”) arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters as further described below,” a letter written by UEFA and seen by the Telegraph, says.

“You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.

‌



“These obligations arise independently of any internal retention policy you or your organisation maintain and supersede any routine document destruction or deletion policies that would otherwise apply.”

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino was forced to perform a dramatic u-turn with the FFE proposals (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The letter continued: “Uefa – as well as other confederations, Fifa member associations and football stakeholders – has strongly condemned the FFE plan in the strongest terms as fundamentally incompatible with the proper governance of football.

“Given that proceedings are reasonably anticipated, you are obliged to preserve all relevant materials (as defined below) with immediate effect.”

In another warning to FIFA, UEFA are quoted as adding in the letter: “Uefa puts you on formal notice that any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment, or loss of relevant materials following receipt of this notice – or following any earlier date on which you were, or reasonably should have been, aware that proceedings were anticipated – may constitute spoliation of evidence.

Article continues below

“Uefa reserves all rights to seek appropriate remedies in the proceedings for any such destruction or loss, including applications for adverse inference orders, sanctions, and costs against the responsible party or parties.”
