Sports.title: Liverpool transfer 'cancelled' as Andoni Iraola proven right with frustrations after U-turn
Sports.content:
Liverpool transfer 'cancelled' as Andoni Iraola proven right with frustrations after U-turn

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has spoken about his dislike for the month of August due to the uncertainty surrounding transfers and one of his players has changed their mind on a move

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is frustrated by the uncertainty of the transfer window (Image: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Federico Chiesa is set to stay at Liverpool for the 2026/27 season under Andoni Iraola after reportedly deciding against pursuing a transfer.

‌



Chiesa has been a bit-part player during his Liverpool career and had been expected to leave in the summer transfer window. Interest from Serie A and Atletico Madrid, and Liverpool's willingness to sell, had combined to make a move appear likely.

‌



However, the Italian forward has gone on Liverpool's pre-season tour of the United States where he has decided he wants to stay and fight for his place in the side. Calciomercato says this is something of a U-turn from the 28-year-old.

‌



Chiesa has just five goals and five assists in 50 appearances for Liverpool following his £10million move from Juventus two years ago. Just three of his 34 appearances were starts last season under Arne Slot's management and a move elsewhere to find more regular game time had been on the cards. But he has two years remaining on his contract and has reportedly decided to stick rather than twist.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Every Premier League summer transfer as Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool splash the cash READ MORE :

Liverpool spent £35m to sign Victor Munoz from Osasuna and remain in the market for another winger, with Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola among the options after the chances of landing RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande receded.

‌



It has been a largely frustrating start to the summer transfer window for the Reds, with the departure of Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards complicating things.

Iraola was brought in after three impressive seasons at Bournemouth to turn around the disappointing drop-off in Slot's second campaign. And, while the Spaniard has been working hard in pre-season, he has admitted to frustrations around the uncertainty involved in the transfer window.

View 2 Images Federico Chiesa now wants to stay at Liverpool (Image: Bill Barrett/Getty Images)

‌



"I particularly hate this month of August because you start the competition, you still don't know if some of the players are going to leave, who is going to come, there is a lot of uncertainty," Iraola told reporters in Chicago.

"It's difficult to build a proper team with a lot of question marks, but it is what it is, it is the same for all the teams. It is the same every season and I particularly enjoy when it's the first of September - done, this is who we are and we build from here.

"But we have to deal with this month of August that I think a lot of the coaches, if not all, we don't like it."

Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes appears to be closing in on a move to Arsenal from Newcastle United

All the latest transfer news with Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool among the Premier League teams looking to strengthen this summer

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Sunday, August 2.

The summer transfer window is full flow with several Premier League clubs beginning to ramp up their business. Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea have made a busy start to the window, while Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United loook set to follow suit.

Mikel Arteta's side look poised to make blockbuster moves for Vinicius Junior and Bruno Guimaraes. The Gunners have reportedly set a day aside for a medical for the Magpies' captain, with reports claiming a bid in excess of £75m has been agreed.

It's been another summer of upheaval at Newcastle United with Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon leaving St. James' Park, with Eddie Howe also leaving the club last week. Lewis Hall and Joelinton are also being linked with moves away from the club, in what would be a huge blow for incoming head coach Matthias Jaissle.

Elsewhere, Liverpool are being linked with a big money move Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain. The French champions may ease their stance, however, with the signing Maghnes Akliouche and a move for Ajax winger Mika Godts.

Sports.title: Arsenal handed Bruno Guimaraes boost as Newcastle change their transfer stance
Sports.content:
Arsenal handed Bruno Guimaraes boost as Newcastle change their transfer stance

Newcastle United have been insistent that their captain Bruno Guimaraes is not for sale, but a transfer to Arsenal appears to be in the works and the Magpies are looking for a replacement

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is heading to the exit at Newcastle (Image: Getty Images)

Newcastle United have reportedly identified a potential replacement for Bruno Guimaraes as their captain edges closer to joining Arsenal.

‌



The Magpies are undergoing a summer of upheaval, with Guimaraes likely to follow Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali out the door after Eddie Howe left his position as manager. Having sold Gordon and Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively, Newcastle had been insistent that Guimaraes was not for sale at any price.

‌



But interest from Premier League champions Arsenal has not gone away and the Brazil international now looks set to make the move to London. The Times have reported that Guimaraes could undergo a medical on Monday with a deal worth £80million edging closer.

‌



Guimaraes sent an emotional farewell message to Howe and is keen to join Mikel Arteta's side. It seems that Newcastle have now been forced to face reality, with the team scouring the market for a potential replacement in midfield.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Every Premier League summer transfer as Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool splash the cash READ MORE :

Corriere dello Sport report that they are ready to challenge Leeds for Inter Milan star Petar Sucic and are prepared to offer between €35m and €40m (£30m and £34m) for his services. The Croatia international has emerged as a key player for Inter and the Italian giants don't want to lose him.

‌



The 22-year-old made 50 appearances for Inter in all competitions last season, contributing four goals and four assists. The Serie A champions value the midfielder at around €45m (£38.4m) and could play Newcastle and Leeds off against each other to drive up the price.

Newcastle have plenty of experience of missing out on transfer targets in recent windows so know how costly they can be. This summer Johan Manzambi went to Aston Villa and Victor Munoz to Liverpool, while last summer Hugo Ekitike and Benjamin Sesko were the most notable misses.

View 2 Images Petar Sucic played for Croatia at the World Cup (Image: Steve Russell/Toronto Star via Getty Images)

‌



Frustrations around losing key players and a lack of incoming transfers is understood to have been one of the reasons behind Howe's departure. Matthias Jaissle is poised to leave Al-Ahli replace Howe and will have a difficult job in rebuilding after the departures of key players.

Arsenal, meanwhile, want Guimaraes to increase their depth in central midfield alongside the likes of Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Martin Odegaard. The Gunners have agreed to sell Christian Norgaard to Everton for £7m in preparation for Guimaraes' arrival.

A £34m deal to sign winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge to replace Leandro Trossard is the only major signing of the summer window for Arsenal. But they are chasing Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior as well as Guimaraes and manager Arteta has promised more to come.

‌



"We are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear," Arteta said after their 4-1 pre-season friendly win over Girona. "We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it.

"The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

Sports.title: Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan
Sports.content:
Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan

Liverpool's hopes of signing PSG star Bradley Barcola have been boosted after reports suggest the French club are closing in on Ajax forward Mika Godts as his potential replacement

View 2 Images Ajax have stepped up their efforts to sign a replacement for Bradley Barcola (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly stepping up their efforts to sign Ajax star Mika Godts, which could hand Liverpool a boost to their hopes of signing Bradley Barcola. The Reds have been heavily linked with signing the France international this summer as they look to strengthen their wide forward options before the transfer window closes.

‌



Barcola’s current deal with PSG is set to expire in the summer of 2028, and it has been widely reported that the 23-year-old does not want to put pen to paper on an extension at the Parc des Princes. There have even been suggestions that Barcola is open to the idea of a move to Anfield, which has given Liverpool encouragement that a deal could be completed.

‌



It has been reported previously that Liverpool are expected to hold talks with PSG over a deal to sign Barcola, with the winger apparently valued at around £140million. That said, separate reports have suggested that Liverpool are optimistic about negotiating a fee closer to £100million for the France international.

‌



Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star READ MORE :

A new development from Fabrizio Romano indicates that PSG are preparing to secure Ajax winger Godts, with the forward being heavily mentioned as Barcola's replacement. PSG are said to have tabled a €40million (£34.2million) offer to bring in Godts, having already reached agreement on personal terms with the Belgium international.

Godts predominantly operates on the left wing for Ajax, and should the deal go through, it would probably fuel additional suggestions that Barcola might be heading towards the exit. PSG are also understood to be nearing a deal to bring in Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco, which would further fuel the speculation that Barcola could end up departing the Ligue 1 champions.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is wanted by Liverpool (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool have experienced a quiet transfer window thus far, with just two fresh additions to the squad that Andoni Iraola took over from previous head coach Arne Slot.

Victor Munoz was brought in by Liverpool at the beginning of the summer transfer window, with the Reds agreeing to trigger the £34.5million release clause in the Spain international's contract at Osasuna.

Liverpool also secured a £60million deal to sign Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes back in February, with the defender officially joining Anfield this summer but has yet to feature during pre-season.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut

Alejandro Garnacho has completed a loan move from Chelsea to Aston Villa and the former Manchester United winger has appeared to take a dig at his former employers

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho left Chelsea for Aston Villa (Image: Chelsea Football Club, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Alejandro Garnacho has claimed he is enjoying football again in an apparent dig at former club Chelsea. The Argentinian made his Aston Villa debut against Indonesia All Stars as Unai Emery's side ran out 3-1 winners but the 22-year-old couldn't resist a swipe at the Blues.

‌



Garnacho joined the Europa League holders on a season-long loan with a conditional obligation to buy for £43million, should Villa opt to trigger it. It appears no love has been lost with his former employers after suggesting he had an unhappy time at Stamford Bridge.

‌



Xabi Alonso made the attacker surplus to requirements after being appointed as the permanent manager. Garnacho, who left Manchester United under a cloud last summer, has sparked another bitter dispute after departing a club.

‌



Taking to social media following their 3-1 victory over Indonesia All Stars, Garnacho said: "First start after three months.

Preston vs Barcelona friendly cancelled hours before kick-off for bizarre reason READ MORE :

Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend READ MORE :

"Happy to be enjoying football again. One percent every day. Thanks Indonesia."

The attacker's stint at Old Trafford concluded on a bitter note before his initial switch to Stamford Bridge failed to come off in January 2025. Garnacho lost favour under Ruben Amorim and was dropped from the squad for the victory over Manchester City, while his omission from the Europa League final starting XI prompted a post-match outburst.

‌



United will be monitoring developments closely as Garnacho prepares for his maiden season in the West Midlands. Michael Carrick's outfit would be entitled to 10 per cent of any future transfer fee for the 22-year-old and should the buyout clause be activated, Villa will be obliged to pay £43million for his signature.

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho appeared to take a dig at Chelsea on social media (Image: garnacho7/Instagram)

.JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Garnacho endured a torrid debut season in the capital, during a chaotic period for the Londoners that saw a string of managerial changes. Enzo Maresca had been keen to bring the United winger to the club but departed in January after 18 months at the helm. Liam Rosenior was subsequently appointed as his replacement, yet his time in charge proved brief, with the axe falling after just 106 days

Alonso was confirmed as permanent boss this summer following Calum McFarlane's stint as caretaker. Yet in the Spaniard's very first move at Stamford Bridge, he showed the Argentine the door.

Emery now faces the task of reviving Garnacho's career after a bruising spell at both United and Chelsea. The Europa League-winning manager said: "We are delighted with Alejandro. He is so talented, young and he showed us his wish to help our project. We are really happy."

Sports.title: Liverpool collapse as Leeds come from 2-0 down to win
Sports.content:
Liverpool threw away a two-goal lead in spectacular fashion as Leeds won the final match of both teams' United States tour 4-2.

It was all one-way traffic in the first half for Andoni Iraola's side as Luke Chambers and the returning Florian Wirtz put Liverpool into a two-goal lead. Wirtz's goal came from a superb Liverpool move involving the impressive Trey Nyoni and Jeremie Frimpong.

Image: Florian Wirtz celebrates scoring Liverpool's second goal vs Leeds

But Leeds brought on their better attacking players at half-time in Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Harry Wilson - and the tide turned - with three goals in 13 second-half minutes.

Brenden Aaronson benefitted from Milos Kerkez's mistake to pull one back, before Calvert-Lewin levelled from Ethan Ampadu's dangerous long throw.

Sean Longstaff completed the comeback with a scuffed finish just two minutes later- before Calvert-Lewin got his second via a carbon copy goal of his first.

Both sides now return to England to begin the final part of their pre-season preparations, with the start of the season less than three weeks away.

The key moments from Chicago...

7: GOAL! Liverpool take an early lead as Dominik Szoboszlai's corner is flicked on by Milos Kerkez, allowing Chambers to smash home.

Image: Luke Chambers celebrates giving Liverpool the lead

14: WHAT A SAVE! Lucas Nmecha nearly equalises for Leeds but his header from inside the box is kept out brilliantly by Giorgi Mamardashvilli.

26: JUST WIDE! Nmecha has another good chance but drags wide from the edge of the box after good work from Dan James.

40: GOAL! Liverpool show their clinical edge as Wirtz equalises after a great team move from Frimpong's cross - after a glorious ball across the pitch from Nyoni.

54: WIDE! Leeds bring on Calvert-Lewin and he gets in behind the Liverpool backline, but cannot convert from inside the box.

60: GOAL! Kerkez gifts Leeds possession cheaply and Ampadu feeds Aaronson to tuck home a goal back for Leeds.

71: GOAL! Calvert-Lewin heads home unmarked at the back post as Joe Rodon headed on Ampadu's long throw.

73: GOAL! Longstaff completes the stunning turnaround as he scuffs home a finish from inside the box, beating Curtis Jones to the ball.

84: GOAL! Deja vu! Calvert-Lewin nods in at the back post from another Ampadu long throw.

Szoboszlai: We have to take care of set pieces

Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai to LFCTV:

"Now we know we conceded two goals from set pieces, we have to take care of them more.

"Last season was one where everything started to be really important on corners, long throws. We have to take care of it, or next season will be the same as last season.

"Set pieces, everyone has to do their job, or we won't concede. We're also human beings, we are allowed to make mistakes. We have to react, that's important. We have two games more before the season starts."

Analysis: Iraola has lots to do to get Liverpool ready

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Look, it's pre-season. Liverpool and Leeds won't read too much into this. But there are concerns for Andoni Iraola at both ends of the pitch.

Yes, Liverpool had a young team out by the time their collapse came - especially given Leeds put their best attackers on the pitch.

But it was very much the story of last season. Two of Leeds' goals came from Ethan Ampadu's long throws, after they conceded 20 goals from set pieces in the Premier League last season, more than any other side.

The goal that allowed Leeds back into the contest came from a Milos Kerkez mistake. Again, mistakes and uncertainty at full-back was another narrative that emerged last season.

There were positives for Liverpool. Florian Wirtz looked sharp in his first 45 minutes back and Trey Nyoni looks like a real gem in the making. He can push Ryan Gravenberch for minutes this season.

But once Wirtz and Alexander Isak came off at half-time, Liverpool never looked like scoring. With a big injury list at both ends of the pitch, Iraola has a lot of work to do to get ready for the season opener in three weeks' time.

Liverpool

August 9: Liverpool vs Monaco - Anfield, 2.30pm

August 16: Liverpool vs Como - Anfield, 6pm

Leeds

August 8: Leeds vs RB Leipzig - Elland Road, 2pm

August 12: Leeds vs Man Utd - Dublin, 7.30pm

Sports.title: 'Missed opportunity' for Hull and Woad for maiden major win
Sports.content:
Charley Hull and Lottie Woad will be left cursing a "missed opportunity" to claim a maiden major win at the AIG Women's Open, according to Dame Laura Davies.

Hull and Woad finished four strokes behind eventual champion Shiho Kuwaki (-5) in tied-sixth as both failed to mount a final-round charge on Sunday at Royal Lytham & St Annes.

Woad started the day at three under but fell away when posting her first over-par round of the week, while Hull could not build on a birdie start as two double-bogeys at three and seven sunk her challenge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final day of the AIG Women's Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes

"They'll both see this as a missed opportunity because five under has won it," Sky Sports Golf's Davies, a four-time major winner, said of Hull and Woad.

"Charley played a little bit in and out, whereas Lottie was really solid, she just didn't hole enough putts."

Speaking to that point, Hull had 17 birdies over the week, trailing only world No 1 Nelly Korda's 19, who finished one stroke better in a tie for fourth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charley Hull's major hopes were derailed after a nightmare start to the final day of the AIG Women's Open

But Hull also posted 12 bogeys, in addition to the two costly doubles in her final round which, if removed, would have also secured her a place in the play-off at five under.

"Charley made a few too many mistakes," Davies added. "And that's just the way she plays golf; she goes full out attack.

"She was pretty disciplined this week, but I think she'll think, 'I was only four back and I should have been in there right at the death.'"

'Major win will surely happen for Woad'

Woad posted a bogey-free 69 in her opening round, but struggled to make further inroads on the leaderboard with rounds of 71 and 70 to follow before fading on the final day.

Image: Lottie Woad posted a two-over 73 on Sunday to see her AIG Women's Open challenge fall away

There's plenty of positives for the 22-year-old, however, with a fifth top-10 finish for her fledgling career that will see her make a debut Solheim Cup appearance for Team Europe next month.

"Woad didn't roll in enough putts," Andrew Cotter said on commentary. "But she continues this remarkable run of three Women's Open Championships played and a third top-10.

"Again she shows her quality and a major will surely happen for her in the future - she's only 22-years-old.

"It's another top-10 but just not quite there on this occasion."

What's next?

Sports.title: Blue Bolt confirms superiority over Precise at Deauville
Sports.content:
Blue Bolt continued her faultless campaign with victory in the Prix Rothschild at Deauville.

Runner-up to Fallen Angel in the Sun Chariot at Newmarket at the end of last season, Andrew Balding's filly has taken her game to another level this term with a comeback win in Listed company at Goodwood followed by big-race triumphs in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Falmouth at Newmarket.

The four-year-old was renewing rivalry with the July course runner-up, Aidan O'Brien's Irish 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes heroine Precise, and at one stage it looked like the latter may take her revenge in the hands of Ryan Moore.

But Blue Bolt was doing her best work at the finish under Colin Keane and lunged late to claim a seventh win from 10 career starts, with Sir Mark Prescott's Coronation Stakes fourth Moon Target bettering that result with a fine effort to finish third.

Balding told Sky Sports Racing: "She's some filly, she really is - and Colin gave her a wonderful ride. It wasn't very comfortable watching it, I thought we were beat in the last furlong, but he's judged it to perfection.

"She's got great physical strength for a filly, that's her biggest quality, and she's got great desire as well. A big thank you to the team at home and Alfie Redman who rides her every day. She's not easy and likes to take control of things, but he's really mastered her this last six months and done a great job of it.

"She likes to get on with it, she's a powerful traveller and knows her strength, so it's about harnessing that in the right direction."

Blue Bolt now looks set to bid for further Group One success in Ireland, with her trainer adding: "The great thing about her is she's effective on any ground, which is a big help.

"We always felt the Matron Stakes at Leopardstown (September 12) was her race this year and we won't lose sight of that for anything prior to that."

Sports.title: Dunkley leads Trent Rockets past SunRisers Leeds as MI London remain winless
Sports.content:
Sophia Dunkley's 56 off 33 balls fired Trent Rockets past SunRisers Leeds in an impressive victory by five runs in The Hundred at Trent Bridge.

Opener Dunkley's imperious innings was aided by a useful contribution from her international team-mate Nat Sciver-Brunt (33 off 25) and a cameo from Bess Heath to leave the Rockets with a middling - but defendable - score of 139-7 after their 100 balls.

Australia star Ash Gardener (1-18) delivered for the home side, taking the early wicket of opener Bryony Smith (10 off 12) and limiting the top-order scoring of Jess Jonassen (19 off 18) and Phoebe Litchfield (24 off 22) to leave SunRisers Leeds well behind the required run-rate at 73-3 off 64 balls.

Image: Phoebe Litchfield managed 24 off 22 before being dismissed by Charley Phillips

Annabel Sutherland, though, reignited hope for the batting side with a brilliant 59no off 30 deliveries, but it was too little too late for the visitors as some tidy bowling by Kim Garth (0-26) at the death - despite a last-ball maximum by Sutherland - meant the Rockets held on and secured an important victory.

The win consolidates their strong position as they remain second in the table, while SunRisers Leeds, languishing in seventh, take another damaging blow to their Eliminator chances.

Manchester Super Giants leave MI London winless

Manchester Super Giants consolidated their third-place position in The Hundred with a six-wicket win over MI London.

MI London, still without a win and planted firmly at the foot of the table, lost the toss and were asked to bat, and it was imperative that they got off to a decent start in the absence of Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who has been ruled out the remainder of the tournament.

Wyatt-Hodge out for rest of Hundred

Image: MI London's Danni Wyatt-Hodge has been ruled out of The Hundred due to injury

England's medical team have ruled batter Danni Wyatt-Hodge out of the remainder of The Hundred.

MI London's Wyatt-Hodge sustained a left calf tear during her innings of 52 not out in a narrow defeat by Southern Brave on July 27.

"Following a scan and assessment by England's medical team, it has been confirmed that she will miss MI London's remaining matches in The Hundred," an MI London statement read.

Wyatt-Hodge has been replaced in the MI London squad by Ella Claridge and faces a race against time to be fit for England's three-match ODI series with Ireland in September.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Blue Bolt and Precise clash again in Prix Rothschild
Sports.content:
We have a busy day's racing on Sunday with Flat action from Chester, Yarmouth and Deauville, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.40 Deauville - Star fillies Blue Bolt and Precise lock horns again

A red-hot renewal of this Group One Prix Rothschild at Deauville where Blue Bolt and Precise renew their rivalry.

Andrew Balding's Blue Bolt saw off Precise when landing a first Group One success in the Falmouth at Newmarket last month and bids to confirm that form under Colin Keane. A dominant winner on that occasion, the market believes she can follow up and land a four-timer.

Balding said: "She seems in good nick and if she repeats the performance from Newmarket she will take a lot of beating.

"She's been a star this year and the only factor is she has never travelled far from home to run before. But if she takes the travel in her stride then she should hold every chance of continuing her winning run."

Aidan O'Brien saddles Precise, herself a four-time Group One scorer, with Ryan Moore in the plate. An impressive winner of the Irish 1000 Guineas, she took the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot before failing to land a blow on Blue Bolt. Sent off the odds-on favourite that day, it will be fascinating to see if she can reverse the form.

O'Brien said: "She's in good form, she was stood in the gates a little bit long the last day and lost a couple of lengths and turned her head a little bit.

"Hopefully she won't do that the next day and give away those lengths. It's hard to do that at somewhere like Newmarket, especially at the July meeting where you are going straight down. We're happy with everything she's doing and looking forward to seeing her again, she's been a special filly for us so far."

Moon Target has two lengths to find on her fourth behind Precise at the Royal meeting, while Green Spirit might appreciate the drop back to a mile.

A deep contest has several with each-way claims including Karl Burke's 1,000 Guineas runner-up Evolutionist.

3.20 Chester - Unbeaten Lifeplan heads the field

Declan Carroll's Lifeplan faces eight rivals as he bids to remain unbeaten in a cracking edition of the Listed Queensferry Stakes at Chester.

Last year's Gimcrack champion has not been seen since landing that prestigious prize back in August and his connections are hoping he can make up for lost time. Stall nine will make life a bit trickier for jockey Zak Wheatley however.

Song Of The Clyde is a top performer on his day and showed all his ability when taking the Listed Carnarvon Stakes at Newbury. Below his best the last twice, he will not want conditions to be too quick.

Hugo Palmer fields Fitzella and Ardisia who are both closely matched on the pick of their runs, while Calico Blue steps up in class for Roger Varian.

12.56 Deauville - Woot Woot, Nicely and Queen Of The Day clash

A strong edition of the Sky Sports Racing Prix Six Perfections where a host of in-form two-year-old clash over seven furlongs.

Christopher Head has never hidden his admiration for Woot Woot and she justified that reputation when winning impressively at Saint-Cloud and she warrants respect on this grade.

Queen Of The Day defeated Woot Woot on debut before chasing home the exciting Avec Toi on her second start and she will find this an easier task.

British raider Nicely stepped forward from her debut to win comfortably at Hamilton and adds further intrigue to this splendid opener.

Best of the rest

1.32 Deauville - Group Three contest with Light Of Dawn representing Wathnan Racing and Karl Burke. Jorolina and Kosuma look useful.

3.05 Deauville - Group Three where Elle Eclipse and Lefteye feature. Evita has good form behind Diamond Necklace. William Buick rides Symbol Of Majesty.

10.09 Saratoga - Grade Two Glen Falls - rescheduled with Survie and Gezora fancied.

3.52 Chester - Power Fizz and Monarch's Gold involved alongside Roman Dragon.

3.08 Yarmouth - Valuable novice.

Sports.title: Thorbjornsen wins first PGA Tour title by two shots at Rocket Classic
Sports.content:
Michael Thorbjornsen made a 26-foot putt for birdie on his last hole to shoot a seven-under 63 and reach 18 under to win his first PGA Tour title by two shots at the final Rocket Classic on Sunday.

Thorbjornsen started the fourth round three shots behind leader Davis Riley, whose rough start opened opportunities for the field.

Thorbjornsen took advantage, surging into the lead at No 14 with his third of four birdies in a six-hole stretch and closing with a clutch, curling putt that went in the right side of the cup.

Sports.title: Pressure on Gianni Infantino increases as Uefa members prepare to oppose re-election
Sports.content:
European countries are planning to increase the pressure on Gianni Infantino with a mass withdrawal of letters supporting his re-election as Fifa president.

Infantino’s reign is in severe peril after the collapse of his privately backed scheme to sell off chunks of the World Cup, which was largely scuppered when Uefa member associations threatened to boycott future Fifa competitions. The mood remains febrile and there is a widespread appetite around Europe to ensure that he is quickly removed from his post.

Now a groundswell of national governing bodies are discussing the formal withdrawal of their support for Infantino in a bid to hasten his resignation, with announcements likely in the coming days. Before last week’s crisis unfolded all of Uefa’s 55 members apart from Germany, Romania and Norway had written letters to endorse Infantino’s candidature next March, with a fourth term for the Swiss viewed as a fait accompli.

A simultaneous withdrawal has been mooted but there is also the possibility member associations could remove their backing one by one. Doing so would effectively amount to a vote of no confidence and increase the pressure on Infantino to resign. Fifa must be notified by any country wishing to recall their letter.

Discussions continue with countries in other confederations. Despite the failure of his Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, a number of countries in the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) publicly backed Infantino over the weekend. Sources within European football have questioned whether those federations have been made fully aware of the level of ­dissent facing Infantino.

After the financial powerhouse of Qatar backed Infantino on Saturday, smaller Asian associations Sri Lanka and Kuwait offered their public ­support on Sunday. The AFC rarely votes en masse however, and it is possible that some associations unhappy with Infantino could rally to the European cause.

As the Guardian revealed in July, more than 200 of Fifa’s 211 members have provided letters of endorsement for Infantino. Fifa is understood to have applied heavy pressure upon those wavering even though his tenure did not appear endangered at the time. Many backed him despite privately offering misgivings about his presidency but, in Europe and beyond, patience has run out.

Efforts to identify a candidate to replace Infantino are being stepped up. Anyone put forward for the election would require significant levels of support outside Europe, particularly from the AFC and the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, Concacaf. Gathering quickly around a suitable contender could be key to persuading Infantino that his position is untenable.

Infantino appears determined to stay on, and is believed to be ­lobbying individual member associations across the globe to ensure he retains their support. Both the ­Confederation of African Football and the South American confederation, Conmebol, are fully behind Infantino however, leaving Asia and North America as the crucial battlegrounds as Uefa members seek a new leadership at Fifa.

Sports.title: The five big beasts are gone: who will be the Premier League’s next alpha manager? | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
This used to be a land of giants. This used to be a land where big men fought. This used to be a land where Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsène Wenger tussled, then José Mourinho joined the fray. This used to be a land where Jürgen Klopp made Pep Guardiola reconsider, and he changed his style and won anyway.

Not any more. Next season will be the first since the inaugural Premier League in 1992 not to feature any of the five big managerial beasts – not Ferguson, not Wenger, not Mourinho, not Klopp and not Guardiola.

What’s come over our great land? The Premier League is still our home, but where have all the heroes gone? Where’s the man who ruled by fury? Or the man who made virtues of broccoli and sobriety? Where’s the man who made the conference room the pitch? Where’s the gegenpressingmeister, or the cold philosopher of the positional game? Now they take a man who instigated some interesting pressing patterns and they call him a regular hero. Where are the men who are willing to play the game?

You don’t have to be a nostalgist in the vein of Bill Anderson to think that the Premier League looks a little diminished. Régis Le Bris took over at Sunderland two summers ago and already he is the fourth longest-serving manager currently at a Premier League club. While his quiet authority impressed last season, the understated Breton is no one’s idea of a main character. And it’ll take a while before the meeting of the two longest-servers, Mikel Arteta and Unai Emery, looks like a clash of the titans, even with the twist that Emery was Arteta’s predecessor at Arsenal.

Tottenham appointed Roberto De Zerbi in March and, the promoted sides excepted, he has already been a Premier League manager longer than 11 of his rivals. All long-running dramas go through this process. Major characters move on, new ones arise. At least they are easier to tell apart than in House of the Dragon: they don’t all have the same hair, and they are not all bafflingly interrelated. Still, it will take time for the new breed to become familiar. Quirks have to be learned, strengths and weaknesses understood.

View image in fullscreen Roberto De Zerbi has the charisma of a leading figure. Photograph: Robbie Stephenson/PA

The result is that this season looks as hard to call as any in living memory. Perhaps the Premier League has entered its Arsenal era and Arteta will soon squat like a giant toad across English football. But retaining the league is difficult, particularly given the emotional outpouring that inevitably comes with ending a lengthy drought. Neither Declan Rice nor Bukayo Saka looked especially fresh at the World Cup, while William Saliba damaged his back. It would be no great surprise if Arsenal started the season slowly.

But who is equipped to take advantage? The previous two league title winners are under new management. Enzo Maresca – Guardiola’s replacement at Manchester City – is a curious manager in that his record is rather better than the experience of watching his teams play. Although his reputation was enhanced by Chelsea’s decline after his departure, it shouldn’t be forgotten just how frustrated Leicester and Chelsea fans became at times with the cautious nature of his football. Arne Slot showed at Liverpool that it is, at least in the short term, possible to thrive when following one of the big beasts but it remains an enormous challenge to succeed somebody who has defined the personality of a club.

Andoni Iraola impressed at Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth, but the truth is that it’s impossible to know how anybody will adapt to the greater scrutiny of a club such as Liverpool, no matter how composed they may previously have appeared.

There’s a lingering doubt about his Bournemouth’s propensity to concede late goals. It may be that a deeper bench offers an immediate solution but equally that could indicate a problem with load management – and that is not going to be made any easier by involvement in the Champions League. Iraola has always relied on extremely physical training sessions, but they will have to be tempered, at least to an extent, by the demands of European football, in which Iraola has little experience.

Similar questions can be asked of Michael Carrick at Manchester United. He did enough last season that United effectively had to appoint him, without doing enough to offer overwhelming proof of his abilities. Signings so far seem to have addressed the right areas in the squad, but the big issue is whether he can handle the demands of playing in multiple competitions. United finished third last season without ever playing a team who had played fewer matches than them.

So demanding is the modern calendar that fatigue may end up being a bigger factor than any manager. If you are a superclub, the key to having a bad season, as United have demonstrated, is to have one so bad that you don’t qualify for any form of European competition.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso endured an awkward few months at Real Madrid but has the time to impose his ideas at Chelsea. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters

Which is extremely good news for Chelsea. Not only do they have, in Xabi Alonso, one of Europe’s most promising young managers but he has time to impose his ideas and his side will be fresher than their opponents in almost every game this season.

Emery’s domination of the Europa League has paradoxically given him a reputation of not quite being of the highest tier, but if Aston Villa can find a way of winning games beyond Morgan Rogers thrashing long-range efforts into the top corner, he has a great opportunity to impose himself. De Zerbi, who has the charisma of a leading figure, should also find himself in the Champions League qualification shake-up given Tottenham’s summer signings and their lack of European football.

The big beasts may have gone but that simply means the Premier League is entering a new phase. What matters now is the battle to be the next alpha. Arteta is perhaps best placed, but the contenders are legion. The land awaits its next giant.

Sports.title: Leeds stage thrilling comeback to sink Liverpool in Chicago friendly
Sports.content:
After 45 minutes at Soldier Field the tale of Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US was of three straight wins and Andoni Iraola’s ideas taking shape thanks in no small part to Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak. After 90, with Liverpool’s expensive duo off the scene, it centred on a stirring Leeds fightback and the recurrence of a fragility that Iraola could well do without.

Daniel Farke’s team staged a convincing comeback to inflict a first defeat of pre-season on the new ­Liverpool head coach. Dominic ­Calvert-Lewin, twice, Brenden Aaronson and Sean Longstaff all scored in the space 25 minutes as Liverpool failed to deal with Leeds’ strength at set-pieces and the disruption caused by a series of half-times changes. The drop-off from Liverpool, who led 2-0 at half-time, following the departures of Wirtz, Isak, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha was drastic.

“Why are there so many fans?” an incredulous Chicago police officer asked his colleague as the crowds descended on Soldier Field, a stadium as impressive in design and location as the skyline that towers behind it. More than 32,000 had been present the previous night to see Robert Lewandowski mark his home debut for Chicago Fire with both goals in a 2-1 win over Dean Smith’s Charlotte FC. The lure of Liverpool and Leeds, even for a friendly, attracted an eye-catching 49,128 to the edge of Lake Michigan.

Wirtz and Isak had missed the midweek win over Wrexham in New York having started pre-season training only on Monday. Ring-rusty or not, they both brought an immediate improvement to Liverpool’s performance level and displayed a rapport that will be crucial to realising Iraola’s vision next season.

Isak looked sharper, more aware of his teammates and more involved in a Liverpool performance than he did during a first season hindered by fitness and injury problems. The Sweden international played all four of his country’s games at the World Cup and, Liverpool will hope, may not need too much time to get back up to speed as a result. That appeared the case here.

It was Isak who instigated the counterattack that led to Liverpool winning a corner having weathered early set-piece pressure. Dominik Szoboszlai took it, Milos Kerkez deftly flicked it across the six-yard box and Luke Chambers lashed in the finishing touch. Isak also led Liverpool’s pressing game with an aggression and relentlessness that augurs well.

Wirtz was involved in much of Liverpool’s best work during his 45 minutes on the pitch. His instinctive link-up play with Isak and Ngumoha, who gave James Justin a torrid time at right back, caused Leeds frequent problems. Liverpool’s second goal five minutes before the break was a delight. Nyoni, who has enjoyed a fine tour at the heart of Iraola’s midfield, floated an inch-perfect cross into Jeremie Frimpong’s run down the right. Frimpong hooked the ball back across goal first time and Wirtz stole in between three Leeds players to slide home. On the touchline Farke berated the officials over an offside call that went ignored in the buildup.

Nyoni, Ngumoha, Wirtz and Isak were replaced as planned at the interval by Ryan Gravenberch, making his first appearance under Iraola, Lewis Koumas, Federico Chiesa and Curtis Jones respectively. Farke also made four half-time changes and the introduction of Calvert-Lewin, the new signing Harry Wilson, Longstaff and Aaronson brought the necessary improvement. The contest was completely transformed.

The Leeds comeback commenced with a mistake by Kerkez. His over-elaborate back-heel was seized on by Ethan Ampadu, who released Aaronson in space on the left of the Liverpool penalty area. The USA international beat Giorgi Mamardashvili with a confident low finish. Calvert-Lewin levelled from close range after Joe Rodon flicked on a long throw from Ampadu and, just two minutes later, a third of Farke’s half-time substitutes put Leeds ahead in slapstick fashion. Jones attempted to sweep away Aaronson’s low cross into the Liverpool area and succeeded only in turning the ball against Longstaff. The Leeds midfielder looked sheepish after the rebound trickled beyond a stunned Mamardashvili.

Leeds were not done there. Worryingly for Iraola, his team were undone by an identical routine to Calvert-Lewin’s first goal. Another Ampadu long throw, another flick on, this time by the commanding new recruit Tarik Muharemovic, and the former Everton striker inflicted more punishment on Liverpool by converting a towering header off the underside of the crossbar.

Sports.title: Chelsea sign Argentina international Valentín Barco from Strasbourg
Sports.content:
Chelsea have signed the Argentina international Valentín Barco from their sister club Strasbourg on a seven-year deal.

The 22-year-old, who played seven times for Brighton including six Premier League appearances during the 2023-24 season, becomes the eighth arrival of new manager Xabi Alonso’s reign.

A versatile player who can be used in central midfield as well as his regular position of left-back, Barco was in the Argentina squad that finished as runners-up at the World Cup, winning his fifth cap in the 3-1 group-stage win over Jordan.

He moved to Strasbourg initially on loan from Brighton in 2025 and signed permanently later that year having helped the club to qualify for the Conference League. In all he made 54 appearances for the Ligue 1 side.

He was involved in a heated exchange with England’s Jude Bellingham immediately after his side’s 2-1 World Cup semi-final win in Atlanta, with Bellingham appearing to clip Barco around the head. The Argentinian, who was an unused substitute, had earlier run on to the pitch to celebrate after Enzo Fernández had equalised. He is expected to join up shortly with his new teammates on their tour of Australia and Hong Kong.

It continues a busy summer in the transfer market for Chelsea as they look to remodel under Alonso. On Saturday they confirmed the signing of the veteran striker Danny Welbeck from Brighton, following the signings of Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Denner, Marco Palestra, Emmanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda have also been signed.

Sports.title: There can be no letup. Humiliated Infantino must stand down at Fifa or be removed | Nick Ames
Sports.content:
There is no time to dance around the subject. Gianni Infantino must stand down as Fifa president or otherwise be legally removed. No fresh chances can be made available for an official who has demolished trust in football’s integrity and governance, trashing all remaining credibility of the body that oversees the world’s most-cherished sport.

Infantino was forced into a humiliating climbdown on Saturday morning when he accepted the failure of his plan to sell off portions of the World Cup to private investment. He resolved to resume dialogue about football’s growth “in the spirit of shared interest in our game”. But such a naked attempt to save his own skin cannot hold. Every day Infantino remains in power is a fresh stain on an institution whose reputation is on the floor.

The overreach involved in unilaterally launching the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme – with its vision to place huge influence on football’s future in the palms of venture capitalists – would be enough to bring down most leaders. But Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond that. He has routinely made a mockery of Fifa’s own statutes and governance regulations, so nobody should be surprised that patience has finally snapped in corridors of power globally. Fifa’s “football unites the world” slogan has never looked more empty.

Article 10.3 of those regulations, which specifically pertains to the presidency, requires the incumbent to ensure “Fifa’s objectives, mission, strategic direction, policies and values are sustainably pursued, protected and implemented, and that a positive image of Fifa is fostered”. It stipulates “promoting friendly and peaceful relations within Fifa”, which is a nonsense given the degree to which federations and senior personnel have distanced themselves from Infantino in recent days.

The rules give no green light to the pursuit of multiple private projects that, most recently in lockstep with the current US administration or its tributaries, have been tabled with scant appetite for oversight or explanation.

Where to begin? The Folarin Balogun saga tipped many leading figures in football, particularly in Europe, towards the edge. There had already been widespread bafflement and disgust at Infantino’s presentation of the new Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump in December, with little background given about the process and highly contestable information provided about the US president’s qualifying achievements. Stakeholders were frustrated by a lack of consultation about the introduction of “hydration breaks”, which fundamentally toyed with the fabric of matches at this summer’s World Cup.

View image in fullscreen The saga involving Folarin Balogun after his ban for a red card was suspended tipped many leading figures in football towards the edge. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

The bizarre expedited bidding process for the 2034 tournament, which resulted in Saudi Arabia’s candidature being waved through in December 2024, also brought widespread criticism. This list only covers the past 20 months of controversies inflicted by Infantino, capped on Friday by revelations that plans for a 64-team World Cup are in full swing.

When a scathing statement from Uefa on Saturday called for an end to “secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game”, it was not only referring to the FFE project and its casual sidelining of other decision makers within Fifa.

A critical mass has been reached. Uefa took a decisive lead in following more than a year of harsh words with strong, united action in pledging to boycott future Fifa tournaments if Infantino did not withdraw his plan. It undoubtedly influenced the outcome and the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, secured an achievement that may define his own reign. But it will mean nothing if Infantino, who is understood to have deployed a major consultancy to smooth relations with federations in recent days, is given the oxygen to dangle fresh promises and turn heads back towards the status quo.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond attempting to launch the Fifa Forward Enterprise unilaterally. Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPA

There is an acknowledgment within Uefa and beyond that the pace must not let up. Senior figures are adamant Infantino must not survive the current scandal. Some insiders feel a crucial next step will be for member associations, the overwhelming majority of whom had formally pledged their support for Infantino’s re-election next March, to recall those letters.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Doing so requires a request to Fifa but could, in sufficient numbers, be a de facto vote of no confidence in Infantino. Fifa had lobbied aggressively for those submissions but many FAs would now be red faced if their expression of fealty towards Infantino was more widely publicised.

Member associations have a duty not to shrink in staving off existential threats to their sport otherwise they, like Infantino, are doing it an egregious disservice. Backing away now would mean leaving the job half done at best.

Uefa have pledged to devise a new method for distributing Fifa’s wealth, delving into its multibillion cash reserves without “selling the family silver”. Behind the scenes it continues to work with other confederations in an effort to find credible candidates for Infantino’s replacement, with a view to running in the election should the Swiss hold on until then. The present crisis can be used to reshape football for the better but only if Infantino is not in situ to impose the final say.

The alternative is that Fifa, and by extension the game, continue lurching from one disaster to the next. It is no laughing matter when the public conversation around football centres on one man, his ego and brazen ventures.

In December Zvonimir Boban, a former sidekick to Infantino as Fifa’s deputy secretary general, told the Guardian that “the way is lost” after the peace prize award to Trump. Fifa will not find a route back until Infantino plays no further part in its operation.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Aberdeen’s late double stuns Hearts, St Johnstone edge thriller
Sports.content:
Hearts’ miserable summer continued as they conceded two late goals to lose 2-1 to Aberdeen in their Premiership opener at Pittodrie.

Wouter Vrancken and Hearts looked on course for a much-needed victory after a turbulent few months as they led through Oisin McEntee’s first-half goal. But just as they looked to be closing out a first win at Pittodrie for more than a decade, Lewis Mayo equalised in the 90th minute before Kevin Nisbet won it for Aberdeen with a stoppage-time penalty after Stuart Findlay was sent off for denying a goal-scoring opportunity.

It was a third consecutive defeat for Vrancken, who has endured a chastening start since replacing Derek McInnes in June. There were five changes to the side that lost Wednesday’s Champions League qualifier at home to Sturm Graz, with the goalkeeper Beau Reus and Laurent Mendy handed their debuts.

In what was their first league match since being pipped to the title by Celtic in May, the 1,600-strong travelling support could be regularly heard singing anti-SFA songs in protest at the contentious calls from officials in the closing matches of last season. There was also a sense of trepidation about the prospect of kicking off the new season at Pittodrie, where Hearts had not won in their previous 14 visits.

Hearts took the lead in the 35th minute after some pinball in the penalty area. Ba-Sy’s cutback from the left broke to Blair Spittal, whose shot was blocked by Nesta Guinness-Walker on the edge of the six-yard box. Dan Happe’s attempt to clear ran into the path of McEntee, who shot low into the net from seven yards.

Aberdeen levelled in the 90th minute when Mayo bundled in from close range after Happe headed Ronan’s free-kick back into the danger area. The dramatic turnaround was completed in stoppage time when Toyosi Olusanya was hauled down by Findlay, who saw red, and Nisbet despatched the spot-kick.

Ibrahim Said netted a late winner as Motherwell started their league season as they left off by beating Hibernian at Easter Road. Said finished off an excellent counter-attack in the 85th minute to secure a 2-1 victory.

The Motherwell midfielder Oscar Priestman had earlier won and conceded a penalty. Lukas Fadinger put the visitors ahead five minutes before the end of a largely uneventful first half. Regan Charles-Cook missed a glorious chance to double the lead before Martin Boyle levelled in the 56th minute after being bundled over by Priestman.

Hibs had two efforts cleared off the line by Martin Moorman before Said slotted home his fourth goal for the club.

St Johnstone twice gave up the lead before storming back to edge a seven-goal thriller at home to Kilmarnock on Sunday.

Josh Fowler gave the home side a 16th-minute lead but Greg Kiltie equalised against the run of play. Cheick Diabate’s header put the home side back in front after 47 minutes but two quick goals from Joe Hugill and Jason Holt – into his own net – somehow saw the visitors lead.

Michael Schjønning-Larsen put through his own net and Kai Fotheringham grabbed a late winner.

“That was a test of character,” said Valakari, whose side came up as Championship winners last term. “Would we be this team who plays nice football in the Premiership but concedes goals and loses?”

The St Mirren manager, Craig McLeish, believes his team’s 2-0 win at Falkirk augurs well for a successful campaign.

McLeish is convinced his squad will improve on last season’s struggles before he steered Saints to safety when the interim head coach. He has set a high bar of the top six and a European qualification bid this term, and a double from Killian Phillips helped St Mirren get off to a fine start at Falkirk Stadium.

“I thought the performance was excellent and if we can build on that we can go and achieve something as a group,” McLeish said. “I’m delighted for the group. We got the result our performance deserved. I thought we were excellent.”

Sports.title: Robert Lewandowski strikes twice for Chicago Fire in MLS win over Charlotte
Sports.content:
Robert Lewandowski scored two goals on his home debut as the Chicago Fire eked out a 2-1 victory over Charlotte FC on ⁠Saturday. The win is Chicago’s first in Major League Soccer since the end of the international break.

Lewandowski, signed in late June as a free agent, produced a vintage performance to help the Fire (9-6-2, 29 points) close an ever-narrowing gap with the Eastern Conference’s top three clubs. Charlotte (7-7-4, 25pts) has now lost four of its last five road matches.

Pep ⁠Biel opened the scoring in the 18th minute for Charlotte. After playing a one-two with Idan ​Toklomati at the top of the box, ‌the Spanish attacker sped past his marker and ‌rifled his shot past Chicago goalkeeper Chris Brady into the top right corner. The goal was Biel’s ‌team-leading ninth of the season.

Lewandowski responded just two minutes later, scoring his first goal in a Chicago uniform. Jonathan Bamba lofted a through-ball to Philip Zinckernagel, who headed it to an incoming Lewandowski. After faking a shot, Lewandowski put the ball on his right foot and slotted into the bottom ‌left corner, past goalkeeper Kristijan Kahlina.

The Fire almost took the lead when Zinckernagel found Robin Lod open in the box. However, the Finnish midfielder couldn’t steer his shot on ​target at such a steep angle, and Lewandowski could not connect with the ball at the far post.

In the 56th minute, Lewandowski played a pinpoint through-ball to a streaking Zinckernagel, setting him ⁠up for a one-on-one with Kahlina. Zinckernagel took one too many touches ​as he neared the keeper, who deflected his tight-angle shot away.

Chicago found the go-ahead goal in the 68th minute ​when Andrew Gutman found Lod ‌just outside the ​box in transition. Lod ​played Lewandowski in with a through ball, and the former Dortmund, Bayern Munich and Barcelona striker beat Kahlina at close range for his second goal of the game.

Lionel Messi returned to MLS action on Saturday, coming on in the second half as his Inter Miami side drew 2-2 with Columbus Crew. The Argentina star could not mark his return with a goal, though, twice shooting wide.

View image in fullscreen Luis Suárez celebrates after opening the scoring for Inter Miami. Photograph: Marta Lavandier/AP

Luis Suárez scored his seventh goal in his last four games to put Miami 1-0 up in the 16th minute, but Casemiro scored an own goal to draw Columbus level. Suárez then set up Noah Allen to head the hosts back in fronts, but midfielder Brais Méndez levelled again with a late free-kick on his debut for the Crew.

Tai Baribo scored in the 77th minute to cap a second-half rally from two goals down as DC United earned ⁠a 2-2 home draw against Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.

Sam Surridge’s penalty and Shakur Mohammed’s strike came eight minutes apart in the first half for Nashville, but Silvan Hefti volleyed in from a corner to make it 2-1 in the 56th minute. Baribo levelled for DC United when his shot from out wide beat Nashville keeper Brian Schwake.
